description: Full-stack test application (NestJS backend + React frontend) to thoroughly test all features of the @block32/jwt-auth package through an interactive dashboard. The backend exposes JWT scenarios as API endpoints, and the frontend provides a clickable UI to run tests and see results.

userStories.title: Setup monorepo structure with backend and frontend
userStories.description: Create a monorepo with two directories: 'backend' for NestJS and 'frontend' for React. Setup root package.json with workspace scripts. Initialize both projects with their respective frameworks. Backend should use NestJS with TypeScript, frontend should use Vite + React + TypeScript. Add the local @block32/jwt-auth package to backend as a file dependency from '../jwt-block32'.
acceptance: Root package.json exists with 'dev' script that runs both backend and frontend concurrently
backend/package.json exists with NestJS dependencies and @block32/jwt-auth as file:../jwt-block32

backend/src/main.ts exists with NestJS bootstrap, cookie-parser, and CORS for localhost:5173
frontend/src/main.tsx exists with React app entry point
Running 'npm run dev' from root starts both servers (backend on 3000, frontend on 5173)

Configure JwtModule.forRoot() with HMAC HS256 algorithm, header storage for access tokens, and cookie storage for refresh tokens. Create AuthController with login, logout, refresh, and me endpoints. Create AuthService with mock user validation. Generate RSA keys in backend/keys/ directory for later use.
acceptance: backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts imports JwtModule.forRoot with HS256 config
backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts has POST /auth/login, POST /auth/logout, POST /auth/refresh, GET /auth/me

POST /auth/login accepts {username, password} and returns {accessToken} in body, sets refresh cookie
POST /auth/refresh reads refresh cookie and returns new access token
GET /auth/me returns current user from token payload
backend/keys/private.pem and public.pem exist (RSA 2048-bit)
All auth endpoints work when tested with curl
